points.description: Part (a), m=n=p=2: valid argument (e.g. expression = (x+y+z)^2 and AM-GM with xyz=8 gives x+y+z ≥ 6) leading to minimum 36, attained exactly at x=y=z=2. Both the value and the equality case must be stated; every step must be valid.

Part (b), general m,n,p with mnp=8: valid derivation (Lagrange multipliers, or weighted AM-GM) with correct final result: minimum = 6·∛2·(m^{2/3}+n^{2/3}+p^{2/3}), attained at x=∛(4p), y=∛(4n), z=∛(4m) (note x pairs with p, y with n, z with m). Must show the point is a genuine minimum or give a valid bound with equality; this value must reduce to 36 when m=n=p=2. The tempting answer 12+4(m+n+p) (from x=y=z=2) or the bound 36 is wrong for non-equal m,n,p and earns nothing; any invalid step earns nothing.

rubric.notes: Full marks need every step valid and both final answers correct, each with its equality case. Part (a) is worth 0.4 and part (b) 0.6. Wrong results such as 12+4(m+n+p), or a bound of 36 for general m,n,p, earn nothing for (b). An invalid step in a part loses that part's mark.
rubric.answer_key:
(a) With m=n=p=2 the expression is (x+y+z)^2. By AM-GM, x+y+z ≥ 3(xyz)^{1/3} = 6, so the expression is ≥ 36. Equality holds iff x=y=z=2. Minimum 36.

(b) Use Lagrange multipliers with constraint xyz=8. Write A=mxy, B=nxz, C=pyz. Multiplying each gradient equation by x, y, z gives 2x²+A+B = 2y²+A+C = 2z²+B+C. Take x=∛(4p), y=∛(4n), z=∛(4m). Then xyz=∛(64mnp)=∛512=8, so the constraint holds. Using mnp=8: x²=2·2^{1/3}p^{2/3}, and A=m(16pn)^{1/3}=4·2^{1/3}m^{2/3}. Similarly B=4·2^{1/3}n^{2/3} and C=4·2^{1/3}p^{2/3}. Each of 2x²+A+B, 2y²+A+C, 2z²+B+C then equals 4·2^{1/3}(m^{2/3}+n^{2/3}+p^{2/3}), so the point is critical. The expression tends to infinity at the boundary, so this point is the minimum. The value is f = 2^{1/3}(2+4)(m^{2/3}+n^{2/3}+p^{2/3}) = 6∛2·(m^{2/3}+n^{2/3}+p^{2/3}).

Check: for m=n=p=2 this gives 6·2^{1/3}·3·2^{2/3}=36 at x=y=z=2. For (8,1,1) it gives 36∛2≈45.4.

Final answer: (a) 36 at x=y=z=2. (b) min = 6∛2·(m^{2/3}+n^{2/3}+p^{2/3}), at (x,y,z)=(∛(4p), ∛(4n), ∛(4m)).
